description: Drug- and scenario-specific clinical safety rules for the clinical-evidence-synthesis quality gate. Kept as data so pharmacists can review, add, or retire medicine/scenario rules without changing server code. Each pattern is a JavaScript regular-expression source. Generic, non-drug-specific safety rules (emergency-call support, exclusive-safety language) stay in clinicalEvidenceQuality.mjs. Supported kinds: report_forbidden (forbid a pattern in the whole report, after optional substitutions), practical_forbidden (forbid a pattern in the safety-first practical section), entity_requires_question_mention (an entity may appear in the report only if the user's question mentions it), practical_required_when_report_matches (when triggerPattern appears anywhere in the report, pattern must appear in the practical section).
routingEntitiesNote: High-risk medicines whose plain mention (with an evidence/analysis intent) routes an open-domain question to clinical-evidence-synthesis, so these safety rules are actually applied. specialistRouting.mjs reads this list; add a medicine here to bring its questions under the clinical gate.

rules.message: Medication response must not be presented as a way to diagnose or exclude the cause of chest symptoms. State instead that relief after a sublingual dose does not distinguish cardiac from non-cardiac pain, cite the evidence for that, and say that persisting symptoms call for emergency assessment regardless of the response.

The practical answer must not add unsupported advice about antacids or waiting for symptom changes. Give only steps carried by a cited claim; if a step seems clinically sensible but has no source in this package, leave it out and say the evidence was not retrieved.
A medicine-free question must not introduce Suxiao Jiuxin Wan into the report. Answer the question that was asked; if the medicine is genuinely relevant, the reader has to raise it.

The practical answer must explicitly state that Suxiao Jiuxin Wan must not delay emergency care. Add that sentence to the practical section — taking it is not a reason to wait, and emergency services should be called at the same time, not after.
